definitions.explanation: The state of being familiar with something or comfortable with it.
A person one knows well; a regular customer at a shop or establishment.

examples.japanese: この{店|みせ}は{馴染|なじ}みの{客|きゃく}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: This shop has many regular customers.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{環境|かんきょう}に{馴染|なじ}みがない。
examples.english: I'm not familiar with the new environment.

examples.japanese: {幼|おさな}{馴染|なじ}みと{久|ひさ}しぶりに{会|あ}った。
examples.english: I met with my childhood friend after a long time.

notes:
COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
・{馴染|なじ}みの{店|みせ} - a familiar shop, regular haunt
・{馴染|なじ}みの{客|きゃく} - regular customer
・{幼|おさな}{馴染|なじ}み - childhood friend (very common term)
・{馴染|なじ}みがある - to be familiar with
・{馴染|なじ}みがない - to be unfamiliar with

KANJI NOTE:
The kanji {馴|な}じむ means "to get used to" or "to become familiar." The word is often written in hiragana as なじみ.

RELATED WORDS:
・{顔馴染|かおなじ}み - familiar face, acquaintance
・{馴染|な}じむ (verb) - to become familiar, to fit in
